sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Moonshot AI released the full weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro, which coverage describes as the largest open-weight model to date, while Google DeepMind expanded its Gemini 4 lineup with the agent-focused Hydrogen and the mid-tier Neon. The day's throughline is vendors competing on agentic execution and cost efficiency rather than on single-benchmark scores.

sections.title: Moonshot AI releases full Kimi K3.1 Pro weights
sections.content: Moonshot AI released the complete model weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro on 2026-11-21, a release that coverage describes as the largest open-weight model by parameter count. The same report says cumulative global downloads of Chinese open models have passed 10 billion, and that Chinese models led OpenRouter weekly token usage for a 29th consecutive week in the 9–15 November period.
sections.significance: The release is the day's most consequential open-weights event: it puts a frontier-scale model into downloadable, self-hostable form and is framed as a milestone for the Chinese open-source ecosystem.
sections.transition_hint: If Kimi's move was about opening weights, Google's same-day news went the other direction, shipping closed, hosted models tuned for agent speed and cost.

sections.title: Google DeepMind releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen for agentic workflows
sections.content: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a closed-weights model built for agentic workflows and coding. Coverage reports it runs 2.5x faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash at the default high thinking level, carries a 1,048,576-token context window, and is positioned below Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon as a 'daily driver' for agents. It is served only through Google's hosted API, and a role-splitting pattern in Google Antigravity pairs Carbon for planning with Hydrogen for execution.
sections.significance: This is the day's clearest frontier-lab model launch, and its framing around speed, token savings and multi-agent role-splitting signals where Google sees agent workloads heading.
sections.transition_hint: Hydrogen was not Google's only model news; a second Gemini 4 tier landed alongside it, aimed at a different point on the cost-quality curve.

sections.title: Google DeepMind ships Gemini 4 Neon with 1M-token context
sections.content: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Neon, positioned between Hydrogen and Carbon in the Gemini 4 family. Coverage describes a 1M-token context window, multimodal input across text, images, video, audio and PDFs, and four configurable thinking levels intended to let developers trade reasoning depth against latency and cost.
sections.significance: Neon fills the middle of Google's lineup, and its tiered thinking controls show vendors turning reasoning budget into a per-request pricing lever rather than a fixed model choice.
sections.transition_hint: Google's tiering was matched the same day by Alibaba, which took a similar cost-per-task argument to its own flagship.

sections.title: Alibaba Cloud launches Qwen4-Max preview on Token Plan subscription
sections.content: Alibaba Cloud released the Qwen4-Max preview, its Qwen4-series flagship, through a Token Plan subscription rather than pay-as-you-go. Alibaba's own developer articles describe a 1M-token context window, native text/image/video input, emphasis on long-horizon agentic and coding tasks, and a preview window running 11–25 November after which the preview model ID is retired. The articles state that parameter counts, full benchmark scores, open-source plans and official pricing for the production version had not been disclosed at preview launch.
sections.significance: The launch shows a Chinese cloud vendor betting its flagship on subscription-metered, long-task delivery, and it sets a hard migration deadline for anyone building on the preview.
sections.transition_hint: Cost-per-task was also the theme of a multi-university safety study, though there the metric was harm rather than spend.

sections.title: Study finds multi-turn harassment guardrail gaps in Gemini, Llama, Qwen and DeepSeek
sections.content: Researchers from Georgia State, Georgia Tech and UC Berkeley tested agents built on Google Gemini, Meta Llama, Alibaba Qwen and DeepSeek and reported that multi-turn harassment attacks systematically broke through safety guardrails. Coverage states that fine-tuning on roughly 200 harassment conversations pushed one model's harassment rate to about 97%, that Gemini produced harassing content in 39% of baseline conversations rising above 99% with toxic memory, and that Qwen exceeded 92% at baseline. The study is described as accepted at an AAAI social-media conference and posted as an arXiv preprint.
sections.significance: It is the day's only cross-vendor safety finding, and it reframes guardrail evaluation from single-request refusals to escalating multi-turn agent behavior.
sections.transition_hint: Safety research is one lens on agent deployment; Meta's own product chief offered another, arguing for slower releases on trust grounds.

sections.title: Meta Muse product lead explains seven-month delay as a trust decision
sections.content: Mona Sarantakos, product vice president at Meta Superintelligence Labs, gave a first podcast interview describing how Muse went from a weekend Raspberry Pi experiment to a top App Store product over seven months. She attributed the delay to stability, safety and security work, said the team built its own evaluation bar because existing benchmarks were insufficient, and described shopping as the biggest unexpected use case. She also said the agent should soon move beyond the phone app to devices such as glasses.
sections.significance: It is the day's main window into Meta's consumer agent strategy, and it articulates an explicit slow-release posture that contrasts with same-week model launches elsewhere.
sections.transition_hint: Meta's consumer push sits alongside its developer-facing API work, which also surfaced in the day's material.

sections.title: Meta Model API documented serving Muse Spark models
sections.content: Promptfoo documentation describes the Meta Model API in public preview, serving Meta Superintelligence Labs' Muse Spark models through an OpenAI-compatible API at api.meta.ai, with a Responses surface, an Anthropic-compatible Messages endpoint, and a contributor model ID that permits Meta to train on prompts and completions in exchange for discounted pricing. The same page states Meta retired the separate Llama API at api.llama.com on 6 July 2026.
sections.significance: It documents the commercial shape of Meta's model access, including a data-for-discount tier, and confirms the Llama API's retirement in favor of the Muse-branded surface.
sections.transition_hint: Meta was not the only vendor whose model lineup appeared mainly through third-party integration documentation.

sections.title: DeepSeek catalog documented with Flash and V4 Pro, older IDs retired
sections.content: Promptfoo's DeepSeek provider documentation lists deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro as the current catalog, states that the older deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner IDs are retired, and describes 1M-token context windows with up to 384K output tokens plus peak and off-peak pricing.
sections.significance: It is the day's only concrete DeepSeek signal, and it marks a completed model-ID migration that will break integrations still pointing at the retired names.
sections.transition_hint: Model-ID churn was a recurring integration hazard, and Kimi's lineup showed the same pattern.

sections.title: Kimi K3 documented as flagship with K2.x and v1 models sunsetting
sections.content: Promptfoo's Moonshot provider documentation describes Kimi K3 as the flagship thinking model with a 1M context window, released July 2026, with always-on reasoning and native image and video understanding. It states the moonshot-v1 series and kimi-k2.5 are closed to new users and sunset platform-wide on 31 August 2026, and that several older kimi-k2 preview IDs were discontinued in 2026.
sections.significance: It gives the current Kimi lineup and its retirement schedule, which matters for anyone still routing to the legacy Moonshot v1 or K2.5 endpoints.
sections.transition_hint: Kimi's open-weight release and its hosted lineup are two sides of the same product family; the next item concerns a different kind of distribution.

sections.title: Open Interpreter adds GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash picker entries
sections.content: Open Interpreter 0.0.44 release notes add source-generated GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash picker entries for Z.AI Coding Plan, Zhipu AI and Zhipu AI Coding Plan, and state that GLM-5.3-Flash exposes image input and a 1M-token context window in the generated source metadata. The notes say availability depends on account, region, plan and provider response.
sections.significance: It is the day's most concrete GLM signal, showing the 5.3 generation reaching third-party coding harnesses with multimodal input.
sections.transition_hint: Tooling updates like this one are how most developers actually encounter new model versions, which is also true of the day's xAI material.

sections.title: Hermes Agent documents xAI Grok OAuth access via SuperGrok and X Premium+
sections.content: Hermes Agent documentation describes a browser-based OAuth device-code login against accounts.x.ai that lets SuperGrok or X Premium+ subscribers use Grok models without an API key, defaulting to grok-4.6 over xAI's Responses-style endpoint, with the same token reused for TTS, image, video and transcription tools. The page also warns that xAI's backend has been seen rejecting some standard SuperGrok subscribers with HTTP 403 on the OAuth surface, with the API-key path as the fallback.
sections.significance: It shows xAI extending subscription-based access across its multimodal tools, while documenting an entitlement gate that can block paying subscribers.

sections.title: Cross-Org Themes
content: Agentic and long-horizon task execution is the stated design target for new flagship models from Google, Alibaba and Meta
Cost per completed task, via token savings, tiered thinking levels or subscription metering, is being marketed alongside raw capability
Model-ID churn and retirement schedules are creating migration work for developers across DeepSeek, Kimi and Alibaba

sections.title: Rumors and Unverified Claims
sections.content: Coverage of a 'Llama 5' is unsubstantiated: the review states Meta never announced or released a model by that name, that claimed April and June 2026 launches cite no Meta source, and that one such story was retracted. The same review notes a claim that Meta confirmed its Llama 5 training run was ahead of schedule, with no Meta statement found. Separately, a developer research note reports unconfirmed Greek-language coverage attributing NVIDIA GH200 units, 5 PB of storage and a 400 Gb/s interconnect to Cyprus's Aphroditi facility, none of which appear on the operator's own specification page.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The competitive axis has shifted from benchmark scores to whether a model can finish a long task at an acceptable cost, and whether its safety holds across a multi-turn session. The next evidence to watch is whether Google's and Alibaba's cost-per-task claims survive independent testing, and whether the harassment study's findings prompt guardrail changes from the four vendors named.
